title: Can image generation help visual reasoning? An empirical study
why_read: This is a careful empirical study showing that having a vision-language model generate a helper image before answering a visual question actually hurts accuracy on 9 of 10 tasks — a counterintuitive and practically important negative result.
analysis: The intuition tested here is that a model might reason better about a visual question if it first generates a relevant helper image to augment the original. The experiment covers 13 model-and-generator combinations across 10 benchmark tasks. The aggregate finding is a 3.7-point accuracy drop, with specific tasks losing up to 10 points. Negative results like this are valuable precisely because they challenge a popular design pattern in multimodal AI, and the breadth of the evaluation makes the conclusion hard to dismiss as an artifact of one model or one dataset.
